text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPEN — high error rate observed for customer Solvix Systems (enterprise-dedicated eu-west). Route: /v1/generate. Paging Sam (on-call). Logs show a spike in 502/504 responses. Please acknowledge and triage.

Sam (on-call): acknowledged. I'm on it — will triage the dedicated pool for Solvix (solvix-eu-pool). Can someone paste recent autoscaler events?

Raj (SRE): looking. Early signal: backpressure on the CPU/IO on node group eu-dedicated-3, pods getting OOMKilled then Retry -> 502. Querying kube events now.

Raj (SRE): quick commands: 
```
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=solvix-eu-pool -o wide
kubectl -n redwood describe hpa solvix-eu-pool
kubectl -n redwood logs deployment/solvix-runtime --tail=200
```

Raj (SRE): logs snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T14:15:12Z ERROR request handler failed status=502 err="upstream reset by peer"
2026-03-17T14:15:13Z WARN kvcache miss spike=0.34
2026-03-17T14:16:01Z INFO autoscaler scaleDown pod=solvix-runtime-5 -> terminated
```

Sam (on-call): hypothesis: autoscaler is overreacting to transient memory pressure and we're entering a spiral (scale down -> cold caches -> higher mem -> more pods die). Can we pin a fallback to hosted model for Solvix while we stabilize?

Ethan (Platform): we have a prebuilt fallback route for enterprise tenants. I can open a temporary routing rule to send Solvix traffic to hosted/medium-latency model (routed to hosted-redwood-medium) for up to 30m. That preserves availability but may increase cost. Want me to flip?

Liz (Account): please do this now and cc me. I'll prepare customer-facing text. Solvix will want a clear impact statement and ETA.

Sam (on-call): do the fallback. Also increase pod memory request on solvix runtime to avoid immediate OOMs. Raj, can you apply a quick patch (scale up with higher mem requests) and hold autoscaler from scaling down?

Raj (SRE): applying patch: 
```
kubectl -n redwood set resources deployment/solvix-runtime --requests=cpu=1000m,memory=4Gi
kubectl -n redwood annotate hpa solvix-eu-pool redwood.io/hold-scaling="true"
```

Raj (SRE): patch applied. Observability: CPU stable, memory pressure decreasing. Pods restarting rate dropping.

Ethan (Platform): routing update complete — Solvix traffic is now hitting hosted fallback. Requests per second dropped error rate from ~18% -> ~1.2% within 90s. Routing ID: route_fallback_sol_20260317.

Statuspage Bot: Draft incident status created: "Partial outage affecting Solvix Systems (enterprise-dedicated eu-west): increased 502/504 rates; traffic routed to hosted fallback. Next update in 30 minutes or when major milestone reached." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/solvix-2026-03-17

Maria (Support): Liz — suggested customer notification below (tailored): 
"Hi <Solvix Ops>,
We detected a spike in errors impacting your dedicated inference pool in eu-west. To restore availability, we've temporarily routed production traffic for your account to our hosted fallback model. This preserves request success but may increase latency and costs slightly. Root cause investigation is ongoing; we are stabilizing your dedicated pool and will resume normal routing once capacity is verified. Estimated timeline for stabilization: 30-60 minutes. We will follow up with a post-incident summary.
If you need immediate support or would prefer we keep traffic on the hosted fallback longer, please reply or call your account team (Liz).
— Redwood Inference Ops"

Liz (Account): LGTM, just add the cost note: "this may incur non-standard billing for routed-hosted usage; we'll absorb first hour, then coordinate any cost adjustments."

Sam (on-call): ops checklist to close: 
- Monitor pod restarts and memory usage (Raj).
- Keep routing fallback for 30m, then run canary revert (Ethan).
- Notify customer (Liz/Maria).
- Create postmortem with timeline and autoscaler tuning suggestions (Sam/Raj).

Raj (SRE): monitoring looks stable. If restarts stay low for 10m, we'll start canary revert: move 10% traffic back, watch errors.

Liz (Account): sending customer note now. I CC support and engineering.

Sam (on-call): noted. tagging next update in 15 minutes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Statuspage Bot: Public status updated: "Degraded performance for Solvix Systems (eu-west). Traffic temporarily routed to hosted fallback. We are actively mitigating; next update 15:30 UTC."

Maria (Support): capturing this thread for the incident timeline. Will add customer responses if any.

Sam (on-call): FINAL NOTE (for oncall handoff): If I'm paged again, escalate to Raj -> Ethan. Oncall shift ends at 15:00 UTC; I'll hand off status to Raj if still active.
